title: Sick with love (10:3, Song of Songs 2:5)
hook: love God like someone lovesick, who can't stop thinking of the beloved
tomorrow: but what if you're only in it for the extra credit?

segments.voice: Yesterday: truth because it's true. Abraham's level, where the reward stops being the reason. Today Maimonides tries to say what that love feels like from inside.

Somebody with a new crush can't concentrate on anything: the phone face-up on the desk, the name doodled in the margin of their notes, every song suddenly about one person. Here's the odd part. That exact picture shows up in a book of Jewish law, describing how to love God. And to prove it, Maimonides quotes a love song from the Bible.
screen: `THE PHONE FACE-UP ON THE DESK.` → `A CRUSH IN A LAW BOOK?` → `PROVED BY A LOVE SONG.`

segments.voice: What is the fitting love, he asks? A love so great and strong that the soul is bound up in it, always absorbed in it, like someone lovesick, whose mind is never free of the one they love: sitting, standing, eating, drinking. Even more than that, he says, should love of God fill the hearts of those who love Him. Then come the proofs. Deuteronomy commands loving God with all your heart and all your soul. And Solomon, Maimonides says, said it as a parable, in the Song of Songs: "for I am sick of love." He adds that the whole Song of Songs is a parable for this. So, the puzzle. Why would a law book reach for a love song? Because a law can command an act, but this command is love, and love needs a picture. The clearest picture of a mind that keeps drifting back to someone is a person in love. He isn't alone in reading the Song this way. In the Mishnah, Rabbi Akiva calls it the holy of holies among the writings. One honest note: some modern readers take the Song first as human love poetry, two lovers among vineyards and apples. The tradition Maimonides draws on hears God and Israel inside it. Here's the thing to tell a friend: in this law book, the measure of love isn't a feeling at prayer time. It's how often the mind comes back.
screen: `ALWAYS ABSORBED IN IT.` · `ALL YOUR HEART, ALL YOUR SOUL.` · `SOLOMON'S PARABLE.` · `AKIVA: THE HOLY OF HOLIES.` · then, large: `SICK WITH LOVE.`

segments.voice: Choose one sound you can hear right now: a fan, traffic, your own breath. Let your attention rest on it, and when it wanders, notice that it wandered and bring it back, gently, the way a mind in love keeps drifting back to one name. Stay with that coming back until the bell.
Sick with love: from the Song of Songs. Maimonides' picture of loving God, a mind that keeps coming back.
Here's the line: sick with love, measured by how often the mind comes back. Day twenty-six, nearly there.

howItsDone: The Song of Songs is read in synagogue on Passover, and some Jews sing it on Friday afternoons before Shabbat; Maimonides' 10:3 is a classic text on loving God.

chat.says: opening night is FRIDAY. i literally dream in cue sheets. is that unhealthy or, like, holy?
options: Maimonides would know that pull: a mind that keeps coming back. He wants it aimed at God, too.
Holy. Maimonides says loving anything that much is the same as loving God.
Unhealthy. Maimonides says real devotion is calm and never fills your thoughts.
chat.meaning: Maimonides pictures loving God like someone lovesick, always coming back to the beloved, sitting, standing, eating, drinking.
